body:
Good question. Here’s an honest assessment of what I can and cannot reliably pull from your GitHub right now.

### What I *can* access confidently

| Content | Confidence | Notes |
|---------|------------|-------|
| Issue titles, bodies, metadata | High | I can list and read individual issues cleanly. |
| Issue comments | High | I can pull the comment threads. |
| Repo file tree & text files | High | README, code, markdown, JSON, etc. |
| Basic repo metadata | High | Stars, dates, description, etc. |
| Search across your issues/code | High | Works well. |

### What is weaker or incomplete

| Content | Confidence | Notes |
|---------|------------|-------|
| **Uploaded media in issues** (MP4s, images via `user-attachments`) | Medium–Low | I can *see the links* in the issue body (e.g. `https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/xxxx`). I cannot always download or fully “watch” the video the same way a browser can. Images are sometimes viewable; videos are harder. |
| Private assets / restricted attachments | Low | If anything is not publicly accessible, I won’t get it. |
| Full binary/file download of large media | Low–Medium | The connected GitHub tools are stronger on text and metadata than on bulk media retrieval. |
| Real-time “everything that exists” guarantee | Medium | I can get a very good picture, but I should not claim 100% completeness on every attachment without checking. |

### Practical reality with your repo

- Text-heavy issues (like #39 governance, #41 petitions protocol, #45 index, #47 Tenacious D, #51 Syncthing): I can get these essentially completely.
- Issues that are mostly or partly media dumps (photos/videos of crows, geese, etc.): I will see the markdown and the attachment links, but I may not be able to fully process every MP4 the way you can in the browser.
- Mistral has been doing a lot of this work already, so between the two of us the coverage on the *textual* record is strong. Media is the weaker joint.

### Bottom line

I am **highly confident** on the textual and structural content of the issues and the repository itself.  
I am **moderately confident** on discovering and linking to uploaded media.  
I am **not fully confident** that I can always retrieve and inspect every MP4/image that was uploaded into an issue the same way a human can by clicking the attachment.

If there are specific issues that contain important crow videos or other media you want me to try to reach, give me the issue numbers and I can test exactly how far I can get with those attachments.
